programme: TP73, HDAC1 and XPC form an oxidative DNA-damage-response axis: XPC senses and initiates nucleotide-excision repair of oxidatively damaged DNA, HDAC1 deacetylation gates OGG1-driven base-excision repair of the same class of lesion, and TP73 sits downstream as the p53-family checkpoint whose own target set (GADD45A, CDKN1A, MDM2, MLH1, MGMT, BAX, CDKN2A/CDKN2B) is the canonical repair/arrest/apoptosis programme induced when damage load is high.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this axis would sit downstream of amyloid- and mitochondria-driven oxidative stress: XPC is reported overexpressed in an Alzheimer-like cell line combining amyloid secretion with oxidative stress, and HDAC1 is reported to modulate OGG1-initiated oxidative DNA-damage repair in the aging and Alzheimer's brain. TP73 recurs most strongly of the three (22/24), but the one paper that directly re-tested it in AD mouse models and human cohorts reports a lack of association, so its role specifically in AD is not established by the retrieved literature even though it carries the target profile of the checkpoint.
role_in_b: In stroke the same class of lesion would arise acutely from the ischemia-reperfusion ROS burst: HDAC1 dysregulation is reported to drive pro-inflammatory microglial activation and worsen post-stroke outcome, and is discussed alongside oxidative-stress modulators (melatonin/valproic acid) and oxidative exposures (bisphenol A) in ischemic injury. XPC and TP73 have no stroke-specific paper in this record, so their place in the stroke side of the axis is inferred from the general biology of post-ischemic oxidative DNA damage rather than from anything retrieved here.
shared_axis: Alzheimer's disease and stroke are both oxidative-stress-dominated CNS/vascular conditions — chronic amyloid- and mitochondria-driven ROS in one, an acute reperfusion ROS burst in the other — so both would be expected to lean on the same base- and nucleotide-excision repair machinery and the same p53-family checkpoint to manage the resulting DNA damage, even though no single retrieved paper studies all three factors together across both diseases.
reasoning: HDAC1 is independently and repeatedly placed in both diseases, including a paper that explicitly ties it to oxidative DNA-damage repair in the aging/AD brain, which keeps the repair module nameable and partly grounded. But TP73, the highest-recurring member (22/24), has a direct AD paper reporting no association rather than one supporting it, and neither TP73 nor XPC has stroke-specific evidence in this record, so the cross-disease link rests more on the general biology of oxidative stress than on retrieved evidence connecting all three factors to both diseases at once.
support: 32424276 — HDAC1 modulates OGG1-initiated oxidative DNA damage repair in the aging brain and Alzheimer's disease, linking HDAC1 to the same repair pathway XPC initiates and placing it in AD. 38329647 — places HDAC1 at the blood-brain barrier in an AD model. 41388741, 42517197, 41136974 — place HDAC1 in stroke via microglial activation, oxidative-stress modulation, and ischemic risk. 26263968 — places XPC in an Alzheimer-like cell line under combined amyloid secretion and oxidative stress. 23414597 — directly re-tested TP73 in AD mouse models and human cohorts and reports lack of association, arguing against rather than for its role in AD specifically. 37081063 — discusses TP73-related lncRNAs in stroke but is not explicit about TP73 itself.
how_to_falsify: Expose AD-model neurons (amyloid-beta or H2O2) and stroke-model neurons/tissue (oxygen-glucose deprivation plus reoxygenation) to matched oxidative loads, then knock down TP73, HDAC1 and XPC individually and measure 8-oxoG lesion clearance and induction of the TP73 targets GADD45A/CDKN1A/MDM2 in both systems. If HDAC1 or XPC loss fails to change repair kinetics in one disease model, or TP73 knockdown fails to move its own targets in ischemic tissue the way the negative AD finding (23414597) already suggests it fails to in AD, the shared-axis account does not hold.
caveats: The blood|brain tissue pairing means at least one side of the 'concordant' call is read out of a non-brain compartment, so activity concordance need not reflect what is happening in affected neurons directly. Only 24 patient-group comparisons from 6 independent cohort pairs underlie this list, and support for the three carrying factors ranges from 22/24 (TP73) down to 17/24 (XPC), so XPC's place in the module is the least secure on the recurrence evidence alone. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed several interferon/inflammation and generic chromatin regulators (STAT1, IRF1, E2F1, E2F2, VDR, HDAC7, FOXO4) common to blood/brain comparisons generally — their absence is a property of that filter, not evidence against an inflammatory story, and this account deliberately does not reach for one. NR4A3 and FOSL1 also survived concordance with stroke- or endothelial-relevant literature of their own, but their target sets point to immune/metabolic and vascular-remodeling processes distinct from DNA-damage repair, so they are left out of this programme rather than folded in as additional support.
